summary.text: A greenhouse Earth is a climate state lasting millions of years in which no continental glaciers exist anywhere on the planet.
In this state, greenhouse gases such as carbon dioxide and methane are high and trap solar energy, and sea surfaces range from 28 °C in the tropics to 0 °C near the poles.
Earth has spent about 85% of its history in a greenhouse state, though today it is in an icehouse state with ice sheets at both poles.

facts.label: Volcanic trigger
facts.value: Volcanoes release heat-trapping CO₂ and methane

items.prompt: Rock records show a stretch of time when no continental glaciers existed anywhere on the planet. Which climate state was Earth in?

options.label: A greenhouse state
An interglacial within an ice age
An icehouse state
A runaway state like Venus

items.explain: A greenhouse Earth is defined by having no continental glaciers anywhere; interglacials happen inside icehouse periods.

items.prompt: Roughly what share of its long history has Earth spent in a greenhouse state?

options.label: About 15%
About 50%
About 85%
About 2%

items.explain: Earth has been in a greenhouse state for about 85% of its history, so ice-free conditions are the usual state.

items.prompt: How does a greenhouse Earth differ from the runaway greenhouse effect seen on Venus?

options.label: A greenhouse Earth is hotter than Venus is
The two are names for the same thing
Venus has glaciers while greenhouse Earth does not
Only the runaway kind is an irreversible tipping point

items.explain: A runaway greenhouse is an irreversible tipping point, while Earth has swung between greenhouse and icehouse states.

items.prompt: A long burst of volcanic activity could help push Earth toward a greenhouse state. How?

options.label: Its ash blocks incoming sunlight
It releases heat-trapping CO₂ and methane
Its lava melts the glaciers directly
It adds fresh water to the oceans

items.explain: Active volcanoes emit large amounts of CO₂ and methane, which can trap enough heat to cause a greenhouse effect.

items.prompt: Both a greenhouse state and an interglacial period are warm. What sets a greenhouse state apart?

options.label: It is a short warm spell inside an ice age
It lasts millions of years with no continental glaciers
It only happens when Earth's orbit is perfectly round
It keeps ice sheets at both poles all the time

items.explain: Greenhouse states last millions of years with no continental glaciers, while interglacials are shorter warm phases within an icehouse period.

items.prompt: Earth is currently in a mild interglacial that began about 11,800 years ago. Which overall climate state is the planet in?

options.label: A greenhouse state
A runaway greenhouse state
A state between the two
An icehouse state

items.explain: Earth is now in an icehouse state with ice sheets at both poles; the interglacial is a warm phase inside it.
